exposure: indications for NICU admission (prematurity, birth asphyxia, neonatal sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome)
cohort: The study included 1043 neonates admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of Mogadishu Somali Turkish Training and Research Hospital from August 2017 to September 2019.
finding: The study found that prematurity, very low birth weight, lack of antenatal care (ANC) visits, and cesarean delivery were significantly associated with an increased risk of neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was linked to a higher risk of neonatal mortality.
followup_time: During NICU admission, within the neonatal period (up to 28 days of life).
birth_weight: The cohort included neonates with a range of birth weights, with 25.5% (n=266) having very low birth weight (<1500 grams).
gest_age: The cohort included neonates of varying gestational ages, with 55.3% full-term, 25.8% preterm (<32 weeks), and 11.9% late preterm (33-37 weeks).
